_what_this_is: Written and committed BEFORE any Phase 1C measurement. It fixes the plan, the pass/fail numbers and what would prove me wrong. Nothing here may be changed after results exist; a change is a new dated file, never an edit.
assets: assets.json (SHA-256, size, ffprobe facts, tag). Original names are not in it. The key (hash -> path) is kept outside the repo and stays closed until RESULTS.json is committed.

primary_outcome.definition: Excess high-frequency energy in the 5-50 ms after drum onsets, measured in the 8-20 kHz band, level-matched and bandwidth-matched, compared with the distribution over human-recorded cymbals.
primary_outcome.bandwidth_rule: A file takes part only if its sound reaches at least 19 kHz (cutoff >= 19000 Hz). Files with a lower cutoff are DISQUALIFIED from the primary outcome and listed in a table.
primary_outcome.level_match: every file is loudness-matched (BS.1770 integrated, same loud-frame definition) before band comparison; absolute band levels are reported next to every ratio
primary_outcome.multiple_comparisons: Holm correction across the secondary measures; the primary outcome is tested alone, at alpha = 0.05 two-sided

loud_part_definition: Frames of 1024 samples, hop 256, band 5-16 kHz energy. A frame becomes LOUD when energy >= the 70th percentile of that file's non-silent frames, and stays LOUD until it falls below the 60th percentile (hysteresis). Non-silent = above -80 dBFS.
intervals: 95 % bootstrap intervals, 2000 resamples, resampling blocks of 1 s so neighbouring frames stay together

1_bandwidth_audit.pass: audit runs on 100 % of assets; on synthetic known-cutoff tests (brick-wall FIR at 16, 18, 20 kHz; MP3 128 kbps; full-band) the cutoff is recovered within +/-300 Hz and classed correctly (wall / gentle / none)
1_bandwidth_audit.wall_rule: WALL = level falls by >= 20 dB within 500 Hz; GENTLE = falls by >= 20 dB over more than 500 Hz and within 6 kHz; NONE = no 20 dB fall below Nyquist

2_metric_sanity.pass: with a synthetic cut of the 5-10 kHz band by X dB (X = 3, 6, 10), the 16-20 over 5-10 kHz ratio rises by X +/-0.5 dB while the absolute 16-20 kHz level changes by <= 0.3 dB, showing the ratio alone can mislead; absolute levels, ratio, loudness-normalised ratio, level- and bandwidth-matched comparison, n files, n frames, medians and intervals all reported

3_line_level_sanity.pass: narrow-band demodulation and the averaged spectrum agree within +/-1.0 dB on injected known 25 Hz lines at -110, -100 and -90 dBFS per line; every line level is reported with its measurement bandwidth; masking threshold and 16-bit noise floor shown beside it

assumptions.playback_level: ASSUMED: -20 dBFS RMS pink noise = 83 dB SPL (a common mixing level), so 0 dBFS full-scale sine = 103 dB SPL
assumptions.hearing_threshold: ASSUMED: Terhardt absolute threshold of hearing formula
assumptions.masking_offset_db: ASSUMED: a noise-like masker hides a narrow tone when the tone is below the masker band level by 6 dB or more

4_synthetic_injection.pass: for each injected effect the measured value is within tolerance of the injected value in at least 9 of 10 trials: air +/-1.0 dB; post-onset HF excess +/-1.5 dB; 25 Hz flutter depth +/-20 % (relative); moving notch centre frequency +/-200 Hz and direction of movement correct

5_sensitivity_floor.pass: for each metric and for the comb, a table of the smallest effect that is detected in at least 9 of 10 trials (shift larger than the 95 % interval); comb floor given in silence (16-bit noise floor) and under loud human cymbals

6_independent_tool_check.pass: headline numbers (RMS, integrated loudness, true peak, band levels) agree between my Python and ffmpeg within 0.2 dB (loudness 0.1 LU); sox is used if it can be installed; Sonic Visualiser by hand is a desktop program and cannot be run here, so it is reported UNKNOWN, not faked

gate_rule: All six must pass. If any fails, Phase 1 stops and the failure is the result.

decision_rules.air_claim: The claim 'v6 has more air than v5.5 / than human cymbals' is DROPPED if, after bandwidth and level matching, the gap is inside the human spread (interval overlaps the human 5th-95th percentile range) or if fewer than 5 qualifying v6-era and 3 qualifying v5.5-era renders exist.
decision_rules.comb_audibility: The comb is DROPPED as a cause of what Steven hears if, in every loud passage, the summed line power in every critical band is below the masker level minus the assumed offset, and in quiet passages below the format noise floor. Kept only if it clears both.
decision_rules.chain_vs_suno: If human multitracks pushed through our own export path or a free splitter show the same swish metrics, the cause is the chain, not Suno, and the project changes direction.
decision_rules.model_claim: No 'the model causes it' without: unit = render, >= 5 renders per arm, effect outside the render-to-render spread, survives analysis on name-stripped hashed copies.

falsifiers: Air gap vanishes after bandwidth + level matching
Metric recovers injected values worse than tolerance (then the metric is dropped)
Swish metrics rise in human multitracks passed through our own chain
Comb below masking and noise floor in every case
Files tagged v6 and v5.5 overlap completely on the primary outcome
The 25 Hz seam click is not found in files where the known-answer test says it should be visible
human_reference_note: Phase 1 uses only the 51 Cambridge-MT stems (3 songs, 44.1 kHz, 24 bit; test use only, never shipped, never uploaded). Phase 2 must add 20-40 references from other source families; three songs is a thin yardstick.
ci_note: CI cannot hold the human or Suno files. CI reproduces only the synthetic parts (checks 2, 4, 5 and the cutoff tests in check 1) using generated cymbal-like signals. Real-file numbers are reproduced locally from the hashes and listed with their SHA-256.
limits: Dates for most Suno files are file dates on Steven's PC, not creation dates. Models are what Steven told us. Neither is checked from the audio.
